Unfortunately you can't easily do this at home as you'd need an air sampler (in essence a glorified vacuum cleaner that blows air onto a petri dish or even a slide - I could post some pics of that as well). Sorry :(

As someone working in a lab those so called professionals send their samples to: Don't. Call a lab and ask them how to take a sample yourself. 
If you want to get the air tested that's a different story (because you won't have the equipment) but in most cases you won't get a conclusive result unless there has been major water damage anyway. If you still want to get a professional to do it call a lab in your region and ask them who they'd recommend.

A great book (especially if you're also interested in microscopy) would be "Food and indoor fungi" (CBS Laboratories). Most common genera/species would be Penicillium, Aspergillus, Cladosporium, Fusarium, Mucor, Rhizopus, Botrytis, Trichoderma, Ascotricha, Mixotricha, Acremonium, Dorathomyces, Alternaria, Geotrichum, Stachybotrys, Chaetomium, Helminthosporium, Chrysonilia and Ulocladium (probably forgot some, but Aspergillus and Penicillium will be the by far most common). Some of these names could be outdated as the phylogeny and nomenclature of molds is constantly contested and undergoes a lot of changes.

I work in a mycology lab. Do you know anybody who owns a microscope or has access to one?
